data.description:
## Observation
While live-probing the sampling fix (tapestried-oversize-blackfly, 2026-11-11), driving `us.meta.llama4-maverick-17b-instruct-v1:0` through rebar's agentic runner on Bedrock Converse (us-west-2) failed with a pydantic-ai Bedrock model-profile `KeyError: 'bedrock_supports_strict_tool_definition'`. Single-turn calls to the same model were not the failing path. Unrelated to sampling parameters.

## Not yet established
- Whether it reproduces on current main (cf7e6e91873 or later) and with the pinned `pydantic-ai-slim` version.
- Whether rebar builds the profile dict itself (a missing key on rebar's side) or pydantic-ai's Meta profile omits the key (upstream defect).
- Which other non-Anthropic Bedrock families hit the same path.

## Approach
1. Reproduce deterministically with a fake Converse client driving the agentic runner for a `us.meta.*` id.
2. Locate where `bedrock_supports_strict_tool_definition` is read and which profile supplies it.
3. Fix on the side that owns the defect; add a regression test covering every Bedrock vendor prefix rebar resolves.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A test that fails on the pre-fix tree reproduces the KeyError for a `us.meta.*` model through the agentic runner.
- [ ] The root cause is recorded with evidence (rebar-side or upstream).
- [ ] The agentic runner completes a tool-using turn for `us.meta.llama4-maverick-17b-instruct-v1:0` (test, plus a live probe recorded as a comment).
- [ ] `make verify` passes.
data.title: Agentic runner fails on Bedrock Llama 4 Maverick with a pydantic-ai profile KeyError
